page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is an x86_64 cloud instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. The system configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage disks, relying on network-attached storage architectures, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate constrained overall compute throughput relative to modern cloud hardware. The platform achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 955.0 and a multi-core score of 2993.0, paired with a stress-ng multi-core result of 4396.19. Memory subsystem metrics yield 33.54 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 28.36 GB/sec on uncached writes. Data processing and compression benchmarks show modest speeds, recording 18.91 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 13.2 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

With respect to operational services, the instance achieved 4.46 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and delivered 3.08 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark database tests registered 1075.89 operations. The primary strength of the configuration lies in its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, trading raw compute power for memory density. This resource profile makes the ecs.e3.large suitable for memory-intensive caching tiers, small in-memory stores, and background data services requiring substantial memory overhead without heavy CPU demands.

The instance features 32.0 GB of memory, creating an elevated 1:8 core-to-memory balance. It does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect conservative compute capabilities, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 2993.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 4396.19, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 33.54 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 4.46 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.08 GB/sec static web throughput. Given the high memory allocation paired with modest processing power, this instance is suited for memory-centric caching tiers, lightweight in-memory databases, and queue workers requiring elevated RAM buffers without intense processing requirements.
